items.title: Jeff Riddick Interview, 1983-08-01
items.q: Now I made a recording on this also with Johnny Wiggs.

ctx.x: 된 stuff... 된 stuff... next 1967. Sherwood Mangiapani had the band. Now this is a recording if ever I cease to love. Music by Rene Luop Society Orchestra. Dr. Edmond Sushan. Now I made a recording on this also with Johnny Wiggs. That seems to be the crop. Pretty good crop. Did you do all the clipping or did your wife make the clippings for you? Don't you know if my wife had made it it would have been in order. But I showed it to so many people you know and everything. It's just all most possible. But someday one…

I wanted to get there with Leonard. We were going out to eat that night. Well, Leonard came there that night and said hello and that's the last of some of them. Yeah. Well, I got to call him back. That's my dear friend. Yeah, he's a nice fellow. I like Len.

items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1969-12-14
items.q: And who's the piano player? Jeff? Jeff Riddick.

ctx.x: Yeah. Emil used to be with the original Dixieland Jazz Band. He was a cornet player before he joined the original Dixieland Jazz Band, and it seems like overnight they made him into a trombone player, the story goes. Johnny remembers more about that than I do. But we had Raymond Burke on clarinet there, one of the... The greatest. Yes. Inventive, creative, always has to play something new. Lovely. Anything you want. And, of course, Paul Barberin on drums. Yeah. Sherwood Man Japan on bass. And who's the piano…
That's what I thought. With that beautiful wide tone. How can anybody get a wide tone on piano? Jeff does.

items.title: Jeff Riddick Interview, 1983-07-14
items.q: he was talking about the different musicians that he'd played with, and when he got down to me, he said, oh, Professor Jeff Riddick

ctx.x: I've heard of him. I just wondered where I'd heard of him. I think Johnny Hyman or whatever you want to call him mentioned him.

They knew each other. Johnny knew him very well because he mentioned him many times. I knew Johnny Hyman since 1926. Johnny Wiggs. That's Johnny Wiggs. Same person. The name you've seen him, right? He said something mighty nice for me the last time I ever heard of him, and this was in the second line. The last write-up that he got. I don't know if you saw it, but anyway, he was talking about the different musicians that he'd played with, and when he got down to me, he said, oh, Professor Jeff Riddick, the old…
There was no, there was a private service, you know. Yeah. His family was strange about that. They didn't want anybody to know.
